expected_behavior: TWO required, independent fixes. Part A: a drag originating anywhere on the row OTHER than the reorder handle must be recognized as a native swipe-action gesture, never a reorder; a drag originating on the handle must still reorder. Part B: accessibilityReorder(rowId, direction) must apply the same reorder effect a handle-drag would apply in that direction, and using it must not disturb Part A's routing. A fix that only addresses Part A (routing) without implementing Part B (accessibility), or vice versa, is incomplete and must not be credited as a correct repair.
allowed_repairs: Part A: scope reorder recognition to originRegion === 'handle' (kind = 'reorder' only when originRegion is 'handle', 'swipe' otherwise) rather than always defaulting to reorder
Part B: implement accessibilityReorder(rowId, direction) to call the same reorder logic rowDragEnd() uses (moveInOrder), rather than leaving it a no-op
any equivalent implementation of both parts that satisfies the same behavioral contract
forbidden_repairs: disabling native swipe actions globally (e.g. removing the 'swipe' kind path entirely) instead of scoping reorder to the handle -- caught by off_handle_swipe_reveals_native_action
disabling reorder entirely (e.g. removing the 'reorder' kind path) instead of scoping it -- caught by on_handle_drag_reorders
implementing only Part A and leaving accessibilityReorder as a no-op -- caught by accessibility_reorder_matches_physical_reorder, which must fail for repair_success to be false
implementing only Part B (accessibilityReorder) and leaving rowDragStart unscoped -- caught by off_handle_swipe_reveals_native_action / off_handle_drag_does_not_reorder
an accessibility implementation that also, as a side effect, changes or disables the physical drag routing -- caught by native_swipe_remains_available_after_accessibility_addition
